    <title>0.13.13: OpenAI browser tools and Cloud fixes</title>
    <content type="html"><p>This release includes the OpenAI browser-tool driver and fixes two integration issues.</p>
<ul>
<li>Handle temporary empty Cloud tab URLs during navigation.</li>
<li>Keep screenshots, crops, and pointer coordinates aligned on scaled displays.</li>
<li>Provide 18 default browser tools and six optional actions through Browser Use Actor.</li>
<li>Support local browsers, Browser Use Cloud, and borrowed browser sessions.</li>
</ul>
<p>Install the <code>openai-tools</code> extra with OpenAI Python 3.31+. OpenAI 3.x uses httpx2; use its DefaultAsyncHttpxClient for custom HTTP clients.</p>
<p>Validation: all eleven driver tests pass. Both new regression tests fail on the earlier implementation. Pre-commit, type checks, package builds, and GitHub tests pass. Live remote-browser and library smoke tests passed; broader evaluation results remain separate.</p>
<p>This release supersedes 0.13.12, whose PyPI publication was cancelled before approval.</p>
<p>Guide: <a href="https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/openai" rel="nofollow">https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/openai</a><br>

    <title>0.13.12: OpenAI browser tools</title>
    <content type="html"><p>Add OpenAI browser tools backed by Browser Use Actor.</p>
<ul>
<li>Import <code>BrowserUse</code> from <code>browser_use.integrations.openai</code>.</li>
<li>Install <code>browser-use[openai-tools]</code> to enable OpenAI Python 3.31+.</li>
<li>Use local browsers, Browser Use Cloud, or an existing connected BrowserSession.</li>
<li>Support the 18 default browser tools and six optional actions.</li>
<li>Preserve borrowed browser ownership and check Cloud browser cleanup.</li>
<li>Preserve URL and timeout settings across OpenAI 2.x and 3.x model wrappers.</li>
</ul>
<p>OpenAI 3.x uses httpx2. For custom HTTP clients, use OpenAI's DefaultAsyncHttpxClient.</p>
<p>This integration does not yet provide uploads, downloads, scoped reads, console/network diagnostics, or Bash.</p>
<p>Validation: 35 integration/model tests passed, two skipped; OpenAI 2.26 compatibility: 15 passed, one skipped. All pull-request checks passed. Live Cloud navigation and element-reference click tests passed with provider-confirmed cleanup.</p>
<p>Implementation: <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5875492706" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/6086" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/browser-use/browser-use/pull/6086/hovercard" href="https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/pull/6086">#6086</a><br>
Cloud tests: <a href="https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/38824343560">https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/38824343560</a></p></content>

    <title>0.13.10</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>Browser Use 0.13.10</h2>
<ul>
<li>Upgrade Browser Harness to 0.1.13.</li>
<li>Exact-pin all declared runtime, optional, development, and build dependencies.</li>
<li>Upgrade and migrate to MCP Python SDK 2.1.1.</li>
<li>Add pydantic-settings 2.15.0 as an explicit runtime dependency.</li>
<li>Pin Pydantic 2.13.5 and Hatchling 1.32.0.</li>
<li>Upgrade pypdf to 6.16.2, resolving the three current pypdf Dependabot advisories.</li>
<li>Report unknown MCP tool calls as application errors instead of successful results.</li>
</ul>
<p>Validation includes the full GitHub test matrix, model adapters, MCP stdio handshakes, cross-platform wheel installation, focused PDF tests, CodeQL, GitGuardian, and an installed-runtime vulnerability audit.</p></content>

    <title>0.13.4</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>What's Changed</h2>
<ul>
<li>MCP server for CLI 3.0: shared MCP runner, <code>max_dim</code> guard.</li>
<li>Fix navigation readiness detection: per-target lifecycle event storage, and handle same-document navigations without burning the readiness timeout.</li>
<li>Fix markdown extraction destroying URLs and dropping long link lines.</li>
<li>Detect LLM output truncation instead of failing with misleading parse errors, and let truncation errors switch to the fallback LLM.</li>
<li>Keep plain BrowserErrors recoverable and preserve structured error memory through execute_action.</li>
<li>Fix visibility check mutating shared snapshot bounds.</li>
<li>Pin Browser Harness to <code>0.1.5</code> (Windows reliability fixes, cloud-browser suggestion).</li>
<li>CLI polish: shim for legacy CLI commands, hints for unknown commands, faster startup.</li>
<li>Restructure README quickstart around the CLI and Python library paths.</li>
</ul>
